source.title: Deep equilibrium networks are sensitive to initialization statistics

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own initialization experiments on deep equilibrium networks, a setting distinct from the plain networks named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports DEQ fixed-point stability and learning behavior under different initialization matrix families, plus test error and perplexity. It does not report training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100. Its practical results on initialization-related learning behavior bear on V4; the DEQ test-error and perplexity results are recorded under fits_no_version because those metrics do not measure the learning-speed or trainable-depth outcomes named by V4. Cited results from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures initialization effects on implicitly defined, weight-tied DEQs, including a ResNet DEQ and a DEQ transformer. V4 names learning speed and trainable depth in plain networks. DEQ training curves address a related question in a different kind of architecture; fixed-point convergence and output variance also do not establish plain-network training speed or trainable depth. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that initialization ensemble affects DEQ statistics and learning stability. Orthogonal initialization broadens useful scales on MNIST; alternative ensembles improve transformer stability and typical training speed without significant gains to best-performing runs. These conclusions concern DEQs.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares random, orthogonal, and GOE initialization families for DEQs, not the plain-network initialization recipes or depth sweeps described in the original-source versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization matrix family, initialization scale, and architecture/dataset: outcomes differ between random, orthogonal, and GOE ensembles and across tested scales.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST, orthogonal initialization gives lower final DEQ test error at larger initialization scales and less variability across seeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Orthogonal initialization broadens the range of initialization scales yielding stable learning in fully connected ResNet DEQs.

fits_no_version.finding: DEQ transformer learning depends on initialization family and scale: convergent orthogonal runs learn faster at scale 0.1, some still fail, and all reported GOE runs converge; at scale 1.0, random initialization reaches low test loss less reliably.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alternative initialization ensembles can improve DEQ transformer learning speed and convergence reliability, with outcomes depending on scale and seed.

fits_no_version.finding: GOE has the lowest average perplexity at every reported scale, while random initialization has the lowest best-seed perplexity. GOE uses smaller dense layers than the other ensembles.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These DEQ transformer configurations trade best-seed performance against reliability across seeds; GOE comparisons also change architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear DEQ output-length variance diverges differently across initialization ensembles near the fixed-point stability boundary; nonlinear fixed-point predictions agree differently across ensembles.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight tying makes DEQ fixed-point statistics sensitive to initialization ensembles beyond their weight variance.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 39th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 162, 2022
record.problems: The practical initialization comparisons are on MNIST fully connected DEQs and a Wikitext-103 DEQ transformer, not the benchmark classification-error settings in V1. The key convergence and test-error curves are figure-only in the supplied text, without exact plotted values. Transformer experiments use 10 seeds, and the text reports substantial variability; it notes that best-seed performance does not significantly improve.
record.rows_left_out: None. Table 1 reports all nine initialization-family and scale combinations, with minimum and average perplexity recorded separately.

untested.parts: All parts: CIFAR training classification error, label corruption, model size, optimizer and stopping conditions.
All parts: teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious minima and student overparameterization.
All parts: depth degradation in plain convolutional networks, identity shortcuts and alternative training recipes.

All stated plain-network outcomes: activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, learning speed, trainable depth, very deep tanh networks and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
All parts: learning-rate stability thresholds, catapult recovery, sharpness dynamics and training divergence.
All parts: batch-normalization speed comparisons, learning-rate tolerance and Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. The supplied text supports qualitative learning-curve comparisons, not exact convergence frequencies. Initialization scale in the transformer experiments denotes sqrt(V), rather than V. DEQ fixed-point instability is distinct from the learning-rate stability threshold in V5.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and the stated size, optimizer, and stopping conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks, depth-related training error, normalization, and the cited alternative training recipes.
Plain-network trainable-depth claims; activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, very deep tanh networks, and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss increases and recovery, sharpness dynamics, and divergence from below the threshold.
Batch normalization comparisons, learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup recipe.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Fully connected DEQs on MNIST at larger initialization scales; DEQ transformers on Wikitext-103 at dense scale 1.00
reader_labels.reason: Orthogonal initialization permits training at larger scales with lower test error, and orthogonal and GOE runs reach low test loss more often than random initialization in the stated transformer setting (r1, r7, r8). The paper also reports faster convergence among orthogonal runs that converge at dense scale 0.10 (r4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: DEQ transformers on Wikitext-103 at dense scale 0.10
reader_labels.reason: Orthogonal runs can still fail to converge, while random runs often converge slowly or fail and GOE runs converge in the reported seeds (r3-r5).
